name: Margin Bell
summary: An SMS character counter drawn as a typewriter whose margin bell rings 20 characters before the end
about: A message box for texting a sale to customers, built like a typewriter. Keys dip and a typebar strikes as you write, the red pointer slides along the margin scale, and the bell rings at 20 characters left and twice when you spill into a second SMS. It counts the way phones do: curly quotes and other special characters drop one SMS from 160 to 70 characters, and the cost for all 240 customers updates live.
how: Type your message on the paper and watch the pointer, the counter and the cost
Past one SMS the extra words are struck through in red: press Trim to 1 SMS to drop them
If special characters are found, press Use plain text to swap curly quotes and dashes for plain ones
Press Send SMS: the sheet rolls up and out, a slip confirms it and a fresh sheet feeds in
